summary: The shadow merge-queue signer gains a third command and timer, seed: on each new tip of main it runs st-test --seed on that commit once, signing and pushing the per-crate rust-tests notes of main's tree for the crates whose key has none, so pull requests branched from main reuse them. It skips a tick while another st-test --seed runs on the host or the host is busy, and its nextest takes the build slots through the admission shim.

replay.detail: No record or signature format changes: the notes are the ones st-test --seed already makes.

schema.detail: No stored or wire format changes; the signer adds a local seeds.jsonl under ~/.local/state/evidence-queue-signer.

rules.detail: What counts as evidence is unchanged: the policy is not edited, and the seed's notes are the per-crate notes st-test --seed makes by hand.

compatibility.detail: Nothing runs until the seed units are installed on a host; observe and sign are unchanged.

manual.detail: On the signing host: reinstall scripts/evidence-queue-timer to ~/.local/bin (it now accepts seed), copy scripts/evidence-queue-seed.service and .timer to ~/.config/systemd/user, then systemctl --user daemon-reload and systemctl --user enable --now evidence-queue-seed.timer. Seed does not need the sign timer.

recovery.detail: touch ~/.config/evidence-queue-signer/off stops all three commands; systemctl --user disable --now evidence-queue-seed.timer removes seed alone.
